card.name: Digits in weight and dose tables
card.fires_on: Single digits inside weight-band and dose tables, such as the 2, 8 or 3 in kg/lb conversions and fractions. It also fires on a few unrelated spots, such as 'or' before the names Seleucus or Antiochus and the start of drug names like Ceftriaxone.

modes.label: Digits in weight and dose tables
modes.description: A digit within a weight range, pound conversion or fractional dose entry.
modes.example: 5 mg in patients weighing less than 40 kg (88 lb), and 10 mg in patients weighing 40 kg (8<<8>> lb) or more.

modes.label: Kings of the North and South
modes.description: Linking words before the names Seleucus or Antiochus in old historical text.
modes.example: 'Kings of the North,' who bore the general name of either SELEUCUS<< or>> ANTIOCHUS.

modes.label: Start of drug names
modes.description: The opening piece of a drug or drug class name such as Ceftriaxone or sulfonamides.
modes.example: receiving C<<ef>>triaxone for injection and calcium
